hints.title: Undirected Graph Connectivity Obstacle
hints.text: Determining whether a path exists between source and destination in an undirected graph with up to 200,000 vertices requires near constant-time connectivity queries. How can disjoint set union connect edges efficiently?

hints.title: Equivalence Partition Invariant
hints.text: A path exists between source and destination if and only if both vertices belong to the identical disjoint set representative.

hints.title: Disjoint Set Union Procedure
hints.text: Initialize a parent array parent[i] = i for all vertices. For each edge (u, v), unite the sets containing u and v using path compression and union by rank. Finally, return whether find(source) == find(destination).

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Alpha is the inverse Ackermann function, effectively constant (<= 4).
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recursive depth searches risk hitting recursion depth limits on large linear chain graphs.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Parent and rank arrays require O(N) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using path compression in find and union by rank.
